On this page, you will find the best gear, trinkets, and best in slot item recommendations for your Frost Mage in World of Warcraft 12.1. From crafted items to advice on how to use your Crests to upgrade gear, we got you covered!

Table of Contents
1. Best in Slot Gear Guide for Frost Mage2. Trinket Recommendations for Frost Mage in Season 23. Nebulous Voidcores (Bonus Rolls)4. Best Crafted Items for Frost Mage5. Crest Usage6. Evaluating Upgrades
1.

Best in Slot Gear Guide for Frost Mage

Welcome to our Frost Mage Gear for Midnight Season 2. Check this page to learn everything you need to know about gearing a Frost Mage, including the BiS Gear from all sources, Raiding, and Mythic+, information on the best Trinkets, Tier Sets, and much more.

Upgrading gear in Midnight continues to use the Crest system which lets you increase the item level of gear along tracks that relate to where you obtained the item, which harder content dropping gear that can be upgraded to higher Item Levels. For more information, read up on our dedicated page on how the gearing system works and what has changed in the Midnight expansion.

OverallMythic+Raid

This list contains the Best in Slot Gear for Frost Mage in Midnight Season 2.

Note that there is no such thing as a singular, all-encompassing "BiS". The best items vary per character and situation, and there are many items that are essentially equivalent in terms of DPS, namely when we are just shuffling secondary stats around. I will list one "BiS" item per slot, but ultimately, BiS lists should be taken as guidance, and you should be simming yourself to find out what gear to equip next.

FAQWhich Tier Set Pieces Do I Want?
For Midnight Season 2 as a Frost Mage, the pieces you convert keep their stats and any cantrip effects. This functionally means that you should convert whatever slots you get at a high item level first. There is no benefit to one slot over another otherwise. You should aim to convert any 4 of these 5 items:
  • Head: Venomkeeper's Horrific Cowl from Ula'tek
  • Shoulders: Brood Cleanser's Amice from Temple of Sethraliss
  • Chest: Primordial Robe of Rites from Altar of Fangs
  • Hands: Grasps of the Eternal Shadow from Coiled Altar
  • Legs: Down-Lined Breeches from King's Rest
FAQWhat Items From the Great Vault Should I Pick?
What you want to take is going to be personal, heavily dependent on your level of progression, and current gear. The simulation result should always inform your decisions. However, there are a handful of items that you should likely take regardless:
  • Jan'thrazet, the Soul Fang: Best-in-slot, and by a wide margin.
  • All of the Venomcursed items are extremely over-budget and worth taking, possibly even replacing a higher track item.
  • Freightrunner's Flask is an extremely good trinket, and very close in value to Wavecaller's Seastone. It is a good pick if you prefer an on-use trinket.

FAQWhich Tier Set Pieces Do I Want?
For Midnight Season 2 as a Frost Mage, the pieces you convert keep their stats and any cantrip effects. This functionally means that you should convert whatever slots you get at a high item level first. There is no benefit to one slot over another otherwise. However, the best in slot shoulder piece, is the actual tier token from the raid, as no other shoulder pieces have optimal stats. Additionally, there are no other cloth Chest pieces other than the tier token. You should convert these items:
  • Head: Venomkeeper's Horrific Cowl from Ula'tek
  • Hands: Grasps of the Eternal Shadow from Coiled Altar
  • Legs: Initiate's Sacrificial Tights from Nek'zali
TipsWhat Raid Items Are Most Important?
If you need a suggestion for coins or if your guild requires a BiS priority:
  • Jan'thrazet, the Soul Fang: Highest item level weapon, with a bonus cantrip.
  • Venomkeeper's Horrific Cowl: Highest item level hat, and the Venomcursed effect makes this an extremely high value item.
  • Aqirbane Reliquary: Highest item level neck, and the second socket combined with the Venomcursed effect makes this an extremely high value item.
  • Gebbo's Bottomless Bag: The best trinket.

Trinket Recommendations for Frost Mage in Season 2

There are a decent number of usable trinkets this season, contrary to last. Wavecaller's Seastone and Gebbo's Bottomless Bag are the solid winners in every target count and talent set, but there are significantly more trinkets than just those that are within a fairly close margin to use.

Frost Mage Trinkets Wavecaller's Seastone

3.

Nebulous Voidcores (Bonus Rolls)

Nebulous Voidcores can be spent to roll for an extra item off the boss, dungeon, or delve you have completed. Which piece you are given is random, but it will remove it from the potential loot pool until you have seen every item once. This allows you to target specific pieces of gear from specific locations.

3.1.

Recommended Nebulous Voidcore Usage for Frost Mage

What item you are looking for is going to depend heavily on what you have, what you need, and what content you can feasibly finish yourself. The priority is as follows:

Voidcore (Bonus Roll) Priority
  1. Ula'tek on Heroic (or Mythic) provides the single best DPS benefit due to the high concentration of extremely powerful cantrip items.
  2. Remaining BiS List items
4.

Best Crafted Items for Frost Mage

Professions are a wonderful way to fill out slots you have had no luck in filling out, and additionally provide a small power boost through Embellishments.

Since crafted gear is time gated, and gearing is not instant, the wisest decision early season is to craft a staff. While this does mean that you end up crafting an offhand later, wasting more Sparks and Crests, it provides the single largest power boost in the early parts of a season. Work on your other Embellished item afterwards.

Frost Crafted Gear Priority
  • Aln'hara Cane with Hunter's Ritual Stone
  • Martyr's Waistwrap with Arcanoweave Lining
  • Aln'hara Lantern after you have obtained your Main Hand off of Ula'tek
  • Any item you do not have on Myth track yet.

A staff, while not best in slot, is still the single largest DPS gain you can obtain early season. Consider holding off if you feel you are likely to kill Ula'tek on Heroic early season and instead go directly for the Off-hand and Belt.

For more information on how you can craft your own gear, you can visit our Professions page.

4.1.

Best Embellishments for Frost Mage

Up to two of your crafted items can be Embellished. This is a similar concept as Unique-Equipped, as you can only wear two items that have the Embellished status. Some crafted items, many of which have powerful procs or beneficial effects by default, are considered Embellished. You can also add Embellishments from a variety of professions to any crafted item, adding the effect to this item either when creating it or at a later stage.

You may also remove an Embellishment that you have added to a piece of gear, if you end up in a situation where you would need to change what item has the bonus, or something gets tuned. This can be achieved by recrafting the first with Lucky Keychain, which will remove the bonus and allow you to craft something else with a new Embellishment.

Currently, the best options are Hunter's Ritual Stone, and Arcanoweave Lining on a low-importance slot, such as Bracers or Cloak.

4.2.

Adding Sockets to Gear

You can add sockets to Helmets, Belts, and Bracers with the Miasmic Jewelbinder consumable that you can get if you do not select any of the choices in your Great Vault. Not picking a choice will grant you tokens, six of which can be traded in for the Miasmic Jewelbinder item that allows you to add a socket to the above piece of gear, if you acquired them in Season 2.

5.

Crest Usage

You will be able to upgrade your items via Crests such as Myth Mistcrest. Once you have upgraded a slot to a certain item level, upgrading other items of that slot to that item level costs no crests.

When you upgrade with Crests, you should think of it as upgrading slots and not items.

Additionally, since Crests are a limited resource, you will want to obtain the highest item-level possible before upgrading a given slot, as this means you will spend fewer Crests on that slot in total. If you are at all capable of doing a +10 Dungeon (3/6 Hero), for example, it would be a VERY bad idea to upgrade an item from a +9 Dungeon (2/6 Hero), because you just wasted 20 Crests that could have been saved by just farming the slot on a +10.

Crests in Midnight are track-specific, so there is no real penalty in upgrading Hero track pieces fully, and in fact can be beneficial as it will skip 20 Myth crests on the Myth 2 upgrade. This amounts to a full extra piece of gear, or a Myth crafted item, every month. For the average player who can only obtain Myth track from their weekly vault, this is a fairly important bonus.

We see a ton of players, even at a high level, mess up their upgrade priorities, and upgrading prematurely. Getting this right will put you far ahead of most players.

Below is the slot priority you should upgrade your items in. If you ever want to deviate from this, you should have a very good reason.

Frost Mage Crest Upgrade Priority Weapon ➜ Trinket ➜ Helm/Chest/Legs ➜ Shoulder/Gloves/Belt/Boots ➜ Cloak/Bracer ➜ Neck/Ring
6.

Evaluating Upgrades

Throughout this page and elsewhere in our guide, we regularly refer to the importance of simming yourself on Raidbots. This is because every character is unique, and each gear piece you have access to can change what is best right now for you.

While we do offer recommendations for gear and trinkets, these are not complete replacements for simming yourself. The only way to truly optimize your character to that degree is by making use of the tools available!
